reason: The cited evidence (E1, E2) shows that mechanically alloyed HEA powders can be sprayed to form coatings, but neither study compares mechanically alloyed to gas-atomized feedstock, measures deposition efficiency, or uses HVAF; the key premises about improved melting, oxidation, bonding, and thickness gain are therefore unsupported by the cited passages.
premises: Mechanically alloyed powder has a more homogeneous microstructure and altered particle size/morphology than gas-atomized powder
Mechanically alloyed powder promotes better in-flight melting and reduced oxidation during HVAF spraying
Better in-flight melting and reduced oxidation improve layering and interparticle bonding
Improved layering and interparticle bonding lead to higher deposition efficiency and thicker coatings
These effects are achievable under HVAF-i7 conditions suitable for 120 mm internal diameters
